name: MRF Ltd (Madras Rubber Factory)
basis: Consolidated (MRF Ltd plus MRF Corp, MRF International, MRF Lanka, MRF SG and its UAE step-down MRF DB-FZCO; subsidiaries' turnover ₹3,974 cr, PAT ₹66 cr in FY26, mostly sales of MRF tyres abroad and coatings)

about.business: India's largest tyre maker: tyres, tubes, flaps and tread rubber for trucks and buses, two- and three-wheelers, passenger cars and SUVs, LCVs, tractors, off-the-road and aircraft; MRF Corp makes speciality coatings. One reportable segment.
about.unitShare: ~31.9% of tyre units sold by the domestic industry in FY26 (~30% in FY25)
about.exportMarkets: Philippines, Bangladesh, Nepal and the UAE; negligible US exposure
about.technology: No technology imported in the last three years; self-reliant in tyre technology for decades (AR FY26 annexure). R&D: ₹255 cr capital plus ₹229 cr recurring in FY26.
about.src: AR FY26 (Board's report, MD&A, conservation-of-energy annexure); CARE Ratings 28-Sep-2026 and 29-Sep-2025

history: K.M. Mammen Mappillai starts a toy-balloon unit in Madras (Chennai); tread rubber follows
Converted into a public limited company
Year-end moved from September to March: an 18-month period from Oct-2014 to Mar-2016 (Screener 'Mar 2016 18m'). Our model history starts at FY17
Share capital unchanged at ₹4.24 cr (42,41,143 shares of ₹10): no bonus issue or split in the ten-year summary, hence a share price above ₹1 lakh

CCI order (dated 31-Aug-2018, released 2-Feb-2022) fines tyre makers for 2011-12 price coordination; MRF's penalty ₹622.09 cr. NCLAT remanded it to CCI; CCI and MRF have appealed to the Supreme Court; no provision made
Raw-material squeeze: EBITDA margin 10.7% and 10.4%, EPS ₹1,578 and ₹1,813 (from ₹3,011 in FY21)
Record margin of 17.0% as rubber and crude eased; EPS ₹4,907
Revenue crossed ₹30,000 cr; GST 2.0 rate cuts (Sep-2025) lift demand in H2; ₹63 cr exceptional charge for the new labour codes; NCD of ₹150 cr redeemed (24-Feb-2026); net cash

fy26.src: AR FY26 consolidated statement of profit and loss and notes 17-23; Board's report

treasuryMar26.care: Cash and liquid investments ₹7,572 cr at Mar-26 (₹5,169 cr); net cash ₹1,462 cr after acceptances and dealer deposits; overall gearing incl. acceptances and dealer deposits 0.29x
treasuryMar26.src: AR FY26 consolidated balance sheet, notes 3, 5, 9-11; CARE 28-Sep-2026

q1fy27.commentary: OEM demand buoyant and replacement robust; price increases and cost measures only partly offset raw material; firm RM prices due to the Middle East conflict; management cautious on demand given the risk of a sub-normal monsoon (MOSL). CARE: PBILDT margin (incl. other income) 13.77% vs 15.35% on sharp rubber and crude-linked increases and the lag in price revisions.
q1fy27.src: Screener.in (as reported); MOSL 1QFY27 results update 11-Aug-2026; Moneycontrol via TradingView 12-Aug-2026; CARE 28-Sep-2026

capex.guidance: None published; CARE expects capex to be funded from accruals and liquid balances
capex.src: AR FY26 notes 6, 25(o) and cash flow statement; CARE 28-Sep-2026

management.board: 14 directors, 7 independent (50%), 3 women (CARE). Executive directors are all from the Mammen family: K.M. Mammen (Chairman & MD), Arun Mammen (Vice Chairman & MD, his brother), Rahul Mammen Mappillai (MD) and Samir Thariyan Mappillai (whole-time director; both K.M. Mammen's sons), Varun Mammen (whole-time director). Ambika Mammen and Dr Cibi Mammen (wives of the two MDs) are non-executive directors.
management.remunerationNotes: KMP short-term benefits ₹162.3 cr in FY26 vs ₹111.8 cr in FY25 (+45%); increases of 33-80% per director; ratio to median employee 271-541x. Terms revised by postal ballot effective 1-Apr-2025 to link commission to profit (s.198 net profit). Total family pay ₹157 cr vs a total dividend of ~₹100 cr.
management.relatedParty: Purchases of materials/machinery from companies in which directors are interested ₹322 cr (FY25 ₹250 cr); services ₹32 cr; subsidiaries ₹3,475 cr (MRF SG, sourcing).
management.auditors: M M Nissim & Co LLP and Sastri & Shah (joint); key audit matters: litigation and contingent liabilities
management.industrialRelations: Cordial except a few work disruptions at Arkonam, Tiruvottiyur and Trichy; Trichy long-term settlement under negotiation
management.src: AR FY26 (corporate governance report, annexure on remuneration, note 27c); CARE 28-Sep-2026

other.epr: Extended Producer Responsibility for waste tyres: ₹150 cr charged in FY26 (₹121 cr in FY25), based on domestic revenue two years earlier
other.importsShare: Imported raw materials 33.7% of consumption in FY26 (CARE); forex earnings ₹2,042 cr vs outgo ₹5,611 cr (AR)
other.renewables: Renewable energy 30% of operations' power in FY26 (24% in FY25)
